PRD · one-click meeting-notes exportv0.3 · In review
Section 1 of 6Background and problem
User interview · project manager

“After six meetings a week, just organizing the notes and forwarding them one by one takes 40 minutes.”

6+ meetingsmeetings per week
40 minutesper round of organizing and forwarding
3 peoplein-depth interviews
Fact · from 3 interviewsAssumption · recipients are the real readers

State who has what problem in which situation, and label what is fact versus assumption.

A PRD aligns decisions from background through acceptance. A technical proposal can link into it, but cannot make those decisions for it.

How a PRD aligns a team on one request

Start with the user problem and goal: Name the user, situation, and obstacle, then state the result the work should change.

Set the scope and non-goals: State required cases, constraints, and what this release will not address.

Agree on evidence: Use observable acceptance criteria or success signals, and keep assumptions and open questions with the request.

What people often confuse

A PRD is not a roadmap, technical design, or wireframe. It defines the current problem, goal, scope, and success criteria, while those materials cover timing, implementation, or screen structure.
